You will assist in the implementation of NAVAIR CM related policy and procedures.
You will provide decentralized management and control of Engineering Change Proposals (ECP), Rapid Action Minor Engineering Changes (RAMEC); Interim Technical Directives (TD), and major/critical Variances.
You will maintain decentralized metrics files of all configuration management and/or Change Control Board (CCB) actions.
You will co-chair, operate and support decentralized CM process activities.
You will prepare and/or analyze new program acquisition or modification for CM requirements, processes and engineering change actions.
You will facilitate the technical and logistics review process and impact on existing airborne weapon systems and commonality issues as related to the CM competency.
You will carry out specific or collateral tasks and functions identified/assigned as CM related, such as the facilitating the review and analyzing retrofit documents.
You will prepare and maintain IPT Configuration Management Plan (CMP).
You will work with NAVAIR required CCB Change Request workbooks.
You will utilize the Enterprise ECP processing tool, currently ePower, for processing change documents.
You will serve as a Functional Configuration Audit (FCA) and/or Physical Configuration Audit (PCA) review team member.
You will also serve as the primary IPT member for CM and carry out assigned tasks and functions across all group-working levels.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11/12 grade level or pay band DA-04 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Utilize a wide range of technical and business systems, processes, and practices used to manage weapon systems acquisition; 2) Review, analyze, and implement higher level procurement policies; 3) Manage project/program requirements, objectives and metrics, and resolving conflicts among schedules, funding, and resources; 4) Identify opportunities to incorporate process improvements and best practices utilizing customer feedback, internal and external audits, self-assessment, and lessons learned activities; 5) Advise management and colleagues on difficult problems, conducting special studies, proposing options and alternatives, and representing a command.

Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Directs the management, integration, and centralization of enterprise data assets, applying modern Machine Learning and Large Language Model principles to drive system interoperability and create authoritative, single-source data repositories.

Manages the complete lifecycle of all IT hardware and software assets, ensures compliance with federal and Department of Defense (DoD) regulations, and serves as the primary liaison between functional areas and the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) for business IT systems.

Formulates and executes the comprehensive AI Strategic Plan, defining the long-term vision for data modernization, and serves as the principal expert for assessing complex data architectures and harnessing AI to optimize business intelligence and process automation.
You may qualify at the GS-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to GS-14.

Specialized experience is defined as: 1) Applying Machine Learning (ML) and Large Language Model (LLM) principles to drive system interoperability and AI-driven analytics; 2) Directing the development, experimentation, and training of data models for AI solutions; and 3) Providing authoritative guidance to stakeholders on implementing autonomous AI solutions and ensuring adherence to ethical AI guidelines.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume.

If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration.

Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission..

A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service.

This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters.

Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave.

The Program Analyst (Performance) contributes to the agency's strategic planning, performance management, and the digital transformation of how the Peace Corps conducts its business. Major duties fall into three areas: 1.

Data Analysis, Reporting & Visualization- Gathers, transforms, and analyzes large or complex datasets to produce clear, decision-ready insights, using AI-assisted tools to accelerate data transformation (e.g., writing and refining queries) while owning the analysis and interpretation.

Builds reports, dashboards, and visualizations using business intelligence and visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) so leaders and staff have ready access to reliable data Responds to data and analysis requests from internal staff, leadership, and the public, tailoring findings to the audience.

Automates recurring data collection, analysis, and reporting to improve speed and accuracy. 2.

Enabling Digital Transformation Across the Agency- Partners with offices across the agency and works closely with the Office of Information Systems (OIS) to ensure the Office of Planning and Performance (OPP) and agency staff have the data, tools, and workflows they need to do their jobs well.

Identifies opportunities to adopt new tools and better ways of working, and helps colleagues learn and adopt them. Contributes to responsible data governance and data-sharing practices in coordination with the analyst who leads that work, ensuring efforts connect to the broader transformation agenda. 3.

Strategic & Performance Planning- Supports development, review, and reporting for agency-wide strategic and performance products, including the Annual Performance Plan, Annual Performance Report, and quarterly performance reviews, consistent with OMB and Congressional requirements and timelines.

Helps interpret federal performance management law, policy, and practice and translate it into practical guidance for agency leaders and goal leads. Supports the design of accountability and strategic-alignment systems that help the agency execute on its priorities.

What We're Looking for in Top Candidates We're seeking a curious, adaptable analyst who is genuinely comfortable using and learning new tools - and who is excited, not hesitant, about working with AI as part of everyday practice.

This role is a strong fit for someone energized by emerging technology; it is not well suited to applicants who prefer to avoid AI-assisted tools. Strong candidates will bring several of the following.

We don't expect any one person to bring them all, we expect the ability to learn the rest quickly: - Comfort using AI tools to support data transformation (e.g., generating and refining queries) and document preparation - Experience with data and analytics tools, and a demonstrated ability to pick up new tools quickly - Familiarity with cloud data architecture - Knowledge of UI/UX and/or data visualization principles - Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software - People analytics / applicant tracking systems (ATS) - Marketing analytics - Survey research - Product development Please note: If you are qualifying based on education or a combination of education and experience, please review the "Education" section of this announcement.

Experience that satisfies the Specialized Experience requirements must be clearly documented in your resume. Failure to provide this information may result in disqualification. Please review the "Required Documents" section of this announcement for further information on resume requirements.

Specialized experience may be gained in the public sector, private sector, or through volunteer service (e.g., National Service programs such as Peace Corps or AmeriCorps, or other organizations such as professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, or social groups). One year of experience refers to full-time work.

Part-time work will be credited on a prorated basis. For more details on qualification requirements, refer to the OPM Qualifications Standards Handbook for General Schedule Positions, available on the OPM web site.

As a Supervisory Management Analyst, you will: Direct, assign, and ensure timely completion of data liaison and governance projects and activities across all TIGTA business units. Adjust priorities and deadlines in order to address priority requests for projects.

When necessary, negotiate with heads of other units, deciding on and/or coordinating work-related changes, and advising superiors of problems. Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of data and artificial intelligence (AI) governance frameworks, policies, standards, and internal controls.

Ensure alignment of data and AI governance efforts with TIGTA mission, strategic goals, and statutory requirements.
You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement. Specialized experience: For the GS-14, You must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service.

Specialized experience is defined as: - Identifying and analyzing data and systems that are necessary for auditors, evaluators, and investigators to meet their mission; AND - Working with IT officials to resolve barriers to accessing data and systems; AND - Developing policies, procedures, and relevant training for analyzing and managing data and system access; AND. - Engaging senior executives to reach agreement on or consensus about complicated data and artificial intelligence governance policy and internal control considerations through effective written and oral communication.

Time After Competitive Appointment: Candidates who are current Federal employees serving on a non-temporary competitive appointment must have served at least three months in that appointment.

In this role as a Dealer Risk Management Analyst, you will be responsible for: Reviewing Internal Risk Controls - Analyzing internal risk management frameworks covering market, credit, leverage, liquidity, legal, and operational risks at Alternative Net Capital (ANC) firms, OTC Derivatives Dealers (OTCDDs), and Security-Based Swap Dealers (SBSDs) to assess their effectiveness in managing firm-wide exposures.

Analyzing Financial & Risk Filings - Reviewing and evaluating monthly, quarterly, and annual regulatory filings containing financial, risk management, and operational data submitted by ANC firms, OTCDDs, and SBSDs.

Engaging Senior Risk Managers - Participating in regular meetings with firm senior risk managers to review business unit risk-taking activities, aggregate risk metrics, independent risk control functions, and control processes supporting enterprise-wide risk management.

Supporting Agency Decision-Making - Compiling findings, preparing written reports and oral presentations, and contributing analytical support that directly informs SEC leadership recommendations and regulatory actions.

Representing the Agency - Interacting with industry representatives and peers at other federal and international agencies to coordinate research, resolve issues, and support the effective operations of your assigned organization.

Major duties include but are not limited to Serves as business intelligence (BI) and data mining analyst, performs analysis to support data warehouse development, deploys BI and reporting tools, and delivers self-service reporting and analytic solutions.

Prepares quantitative and qualitative analyses and research studies to include a wide array of benefits and health care-related issues. Prepares reports and maintain records as requested, and participate in the coordination, preparation, presentation, and communication of work-related information to the supervisor and appropriate stakeholders. Develops procedures and recommends quality improvements in data collection and statistical information systems. Develops computer-programming applications to automate routine data query and extraction. Provides data processing support for VA surveys, program evaluation, and special studies.

As a MANAGEMENT ANALYST, GS-0343-10, you will retrieve and analyze maintenance data, present results to management; interprets findings from maintenance data and the use of statistical techniques; identifies trends and significant deviations from plans, schedules, and workload estimates; analyzes deficiencies in areas such as material consumption and training, workload, scheduling, management, and maintenance resources use; analyzes impact on the maintenance mission and the results of corrective actions; prepares written reports of analyses and studies; capture specific data monthly for inclusion into the Aircraft Predictive Model (APM) requirement and Readiness Informed Metric (RIM); designs summary reports to meet recurring management needs; controls, manages and maintains the Maintenance Information System(s) (MIS); develops policies and procedures for MIS application within maintenance activities; oversees the identification and correction of file errors within the database; controls, develops and coordinates maintenance data systems and requirements; determines data processing requirements and relates functional aspects to specific hardware and software capabilities; controls automated management product retrieval and advises maintenance supervision on automated information use; identifies data system problems, coordinating with data automation monitors, and submits system deficiency reports; identifies new information requirements, submits information system requirement documents, and coordinates with data system development services for implementing new programs; manage the Data Integrity Team (DIT) program for the Maintenance Group Commander and provide updates and metrics to maintenance supervision; responsible for building, analyzing, and programing system queries to generate local and command level data reports for consumption and information generation in multiple systems; senior level requests ranging from senior wing leadership, the NGB, and MAJCOM levels; conducts Special Studies to assess Health of the Unit Readiness (HUR) / Health of Fleet (HOF); performs in-depth comprehensive analysis of complex and prioritized unit readiness issues; in addition, develops a semi-annual report for presentation to senior leadership; develops complex problem solutions to address and resolve readiness issues as the Office of Primary Responsibility (OPR), while utilizing specific training and knowledge to develop a comprehensive readiness management plan; collect specific metrics for inclusion into the RIM/7401 monthly report, while searching for trends and validating accuracy; analyzes performance data to determine manpower, equipment, and facilities maintenance capabilities; provides in-depth analysis of maintenance manning and equipment, material and facility limitations to determine the impact each has on unit and mission effectiveness; isolates trends and determines material and personnel efficiency and effectiveness; develops methods for improving maintenance planning and personnel efficiency and effectiveness; develops methods for improving maintenance planning and programming procedures to ensure optimum use of maintenance resources; perform other duties as assigned.
Minimum Requirements: Experience, education, or training in administrative, professional, investigative, technical or other responsible work which demonstrates analytical ability and a practical and theoretical knowledge of the functions, processes and principles of management. Experience using computer and automation systems.

Specialized Experience: Must have at least 24 months experience which has provided a working knowledge of the National Guard organizational structures, functions, procedures, and techniques. Experience analyzing, interpreting and developing policies and procedures of local management.

As a Program Analyst (Financial Program Analyst), GS-0343-12, your typical work assignments may include: Preparing recurring and ad hoc travel obligation and expenditures reports and provide monthly financial reporting and analysis report to the Budget Team to support budget planning, monitoring and decision making.

Providing support to improve the accuracy and completeness of requisition submissions, enhance compliance with procurement requirements and reduce processing delays. Compiling financial data and preparing variety of ad hoc and reoccurring reports to analyze and resolve reporting issues.

Working closely with the NLRB Ethics office, the Nonfederal Sponsors and travelers to coordinate and track reimbursement requests, reconcile expenses, and ensure compliance with applicable policies and reporting requirements.
All qualifications and eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the announcement. IDEAL CANDIDATE STATEMENT The ideal candidate for the Program Analyst (Financial Program Analyst) will have experience working with and analyzing travel reports.

Knowledge of travel policies and guidelines to ensure compliance throughout organizations. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to interact with stakeholders, senior level management, and colleagues; and strong analytical skills are desired.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Applicants must have one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-11 grade level, which has provided them with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the Program Analyst (Financial Program Analyst) at the GS-12 grade level.

Specialized experience includes: Experience tracking travel requests through automated systems and responding to travel inquiries; and Experience updating and implementing travel policy; and Experience overseeing the requisitions process to ensure compliance with organizational and budget guidelines.

This experience must be fully supported and articulated in your resume to receive consideration. Please do not cut and paste the specialized experience from this announcement into your resume, as this will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record.

In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above.

Nachhaltiges Schnittstellenmanagement: Du pflegst und entwickelst alle relevanten Schnittstellen wie Fahrplanmanagement, Börsen, Broker und Abrechnungssysteme weiter.
P rozessanalyse und Konfiguration: Du übernimmst das Überwachen, Konfigurieren und Weiterentwickeln von Geschäftsprozessen direkt in den Systemoberflächen.

Qualitätssicherung und Dokumentation: Du übernehmst verlässlich das Release-, Patch- und Testmanagement und erstellst lückenlose Betriebs- und Projektdokumentationen.
Qualifikation

Ausbildung oder Studium: Abschluss in Wirtschaft, Informatik, Mathematik oder eine vergleichbare IT-Qualifikation.
Branchenerfahrung: Mindestens zwei bis drei Jahre Praxis im Energiegroßhandel oder dem Portfolio-Management.
Fachwissen: Verständnis von Handelsprozessen wie Hedging, Herkunftsnachweisen und der Price Forward Curve.
System-Affinität: Erfahrung mit ETRM-Systemen (Soptim, Kisters, Robotron oder Allegro) und gute Excel-Kenntnisse.
Technische Grundkenntnisse: Verständnis für Datenbankabfragen (SQL) sowie erste Programmierkenntnisse von Vorteil.
Kommunikation und Teamgeist: Fließendes Deutsch ab B2-Niveau, gute Englischkenntnisse sowie ausgeprägte soziale Kompetenz.

Attraktives Vergütungspaket: Sicheres Gehalt im Tarifvertrag GWE von 75.000 EUR bis 95.000 EUR je nach Berufserfahrung in Vollzeit bei einer 38-Stunden-Woche.
Planbare Gehaltsentwicklung : Verlässliche Tarifverhandlungen alle zwei Jahre und automatische, strukturierte Gehaltsschritte nach drei Jahren Betriebszugehörigkeit.
Maximale Zeitflexibilität und Remote: Eine 38-Stunden-Woche in Vollzeit mit flexibler Gleitzeit von 7 bis 19 Uhr, ein transparentes Überstunden-Zeitkonto sowie bis zu 80% Remote-Anteil (mindestens 1 Tag pro Woche vor Ort).

Being a Supervisory Program Analyst (Inspections) makes you a valuable member of the DHS OIG Office of Inspector General.

Typical assignments include: Develops or modifies objectives, work plans, guidelines, scope, methods, staff requirements, and time schedules to meet project needs. Oversees report preparation and ensures effectiveness of presentation, adequacy of supporting data, and conformance with policies and standards.

Develops annual and long-range project plans, provides technical advice and guidance to subordinate staff for project activities and coordination functions, and maintains close liaison with Department program and management officials in the areas of assigned responsibility.

Reviews proposals and analytical questions, work papers, and reports to ensure, (a) adherence to the work plan and prescribed policies and standards, and (b) the quality and effectiveness (especially in the areas of content, clarity, and conciseness) of individual work products.

Directs revisions, or other corrective actions, to draft reports and testimony, where deemed necessary. Other duties as assigned.

Monatliches Kosten-Screening & BWA-Aufbereitung: Detaillierte Analyse der Kostenpositionen und proaktives Aufzeigen von Optimierungsmöglichkeiten.
Stakeholder-Management: Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Sales (Provisionsberechnungen im CRM), Marketing (Tracking & Budgetfreigaben), Product (Produktmetriken) und Customer Success (Churn-Analyse).
Accounting- & Controlling-Optimierung: Enger Austausch mit dem Buchhaltungsteam, Prozessoptimierung und Prüfung gebuchter Positionen.
Koordination von Banken & Versicherungen: Verwaltung mehrerer Bankkonten und regelmäßige Prüfung von Anlagen (Tagesgeld, Versicherungen etc.).

Sicherer Umgang mit KPIs, Reporting und datenbasierten Empfehlungen
Sicheres Englisch für eine mögliche Internationalisierung

AstraZeneca is a global, innovation-driven biopharmaceutical business that focuses on the discovery, development and commercialization of prescription medicines for some of the world's most serious diseases. But we're more than one of the world's leading pharmaceutical companies.

At AstraZeneca, we're proud to have a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration. Here, employees are empowered to express diverse perspectives - and are made to feel valued, energized and rewarded for their ideas and creativity.
Global Financial Services (GFS) was formed in Q3 2018 through the merger of Global Finance Operations, Integrated Finance Solutions and Cash Generation. GFS is at the heart of the Finance function - accountable to the AstraZeneca (AZ) Group for the design and delivery of high quality, simple to operate transactional finance processes that enable our customers to focus on AZ’s strategic priorities.
Our processes cover record to report, purchase to pay, order to cash, controllership, financial planning and analysis and finance operations, and we drive AZ’s cash focus through disciplined management of supplier and customer payment terms and practices.
GFS operates globally through a combination of in-house captive and offshored business process outsourcing (BPO). The BPO element has been provided in partnership with our service provider partner Genpact since 2008.
AZ Finance is part way through an ambitious, broad ranging, multi-year transformation programme, called Finance Transformation (FT). FT plans for transactional process and technology improvements will underpin a next wave of GFO transformation and a step change in service effectiveness and efficiency.
Role Profile
The Operations & Enabling Team will establish best practice across the Operations site network, Central Operations, in all manufacturing sites related processes. Your primary focus will be on serving the finance business partners as well as providing support to GFS colleagues.

You will be working in a large team to provide support to the Manufacturing/Quality sites of the Biologics and Small Molecules regions including cost analysis, inventory, and capital expenditures.
Perform monthly journal entries including accruals, reclasses, deferral and release of Manufacturing variances, stock provision or any other ad hoc entry to ensure accuracy in the financial information.
Execute month-end activities as well as financial reporting and variation analysis activities and related deliverables in a timely and accurate manner, including business insightful commentary for the management information pack.
Ensure data across reporting platforms is consistent to guarantee safe decision making for senior management.
Perform monthly/weekly analysis of the Manufacturing, Manpower and Opex, Logistics, Capex and/or Inventory Variances that occur in the site to provide a proper visibility to site Finance and take any necessary actions if required.
Execute all planning cycle processes (manufacturing, site cost, inventory, Logistics and/or Capex) according to the AZ guidelines including the management information pack and analysis of any variations between the different forecast cycles. Also, ad/hoc support with different analysis required by Embedded Finance for decision making.
Provide support and business insights (when possible) with the financial reporting/analysis requests from site Finance.
To build and maintain a strong and effective relationship with Embedded Finance and Finance Senior Management.
Become planning champions (site cost, manufacturing, inventory, Logistics, and/or capex) to ensure all planning deliverables are fully coordinated and ensuring they are clear and performed as per the planning calendar.
Perform all month-end close controls (SOX and non-SOX) with quality and ensuring they are appropriate and as per audit requirements.
Provide support to the Financial Analysts related to month end closing or planning deliverables.
Cross train with other Analysts to provide back up.
Collaborate with external and internal auditors to provide necessary information during the audits that are performed during the year. Guide walkthrough sessions with auditors of key processes (MPC005-01, MPC005-02 & MPC004-01)
Work with the continuous improvement initiatives to ensure implementation of the process improvements within the accounting/finance department, including initiatives to streamline close.
Ensure all relevant processes are properly documented and that documentation is up to date to ensure a proper business continuity process.
Might (based on operational needs) manage interns ensuring they deliver with quality, and they have the right balance of workload and growth in the team.
Proactively build business acumen, understand how information flows from end to end within Operations as well as in the plants.
Attend to Global Planning and Actuals meetings is required (such as Lean P&L, Check-in Planning calendar).
Adopt any Global initiative or implementation and ensure smooth transition of the tools, changes or projects (Manpower Tool, Flex form, Axial, etc) by active participating during testing phase and providing constructive feedback.
Essential
4+ years accounting/cost/FP&A experience where applicable.
English Language proficiency, both verbal and written, with the confidence to express clear opinions and ability to explain financial issues to non-financial management.
Experience in three of Operations core processes (Manufacturing, Site cost, Product Costing, Inventory and/or Capex).

Senior Technical Business Analyst Digital Identity \& Open Banking (a) (80\-100%)
=================================================================================
Die Kantonalbank ist die zweitgrösste Universalbank und die grösste Kantonalbank der Schweiz. Mit starker regionaler Verankerung im Wirtschaftsraum Zürich steht sie seit über 150 Jahren für Stabilität, Vertrauen und nachhaltiges Handeln. Sie verbindet wirtschaftliche Stabilität und langfristige Orientierung mit der konsequenten Weiterentwicklung ihrer Angebote. Das Ziel: persönlich wie digital ein überzeugendes Kundenerlebnis zu bieten.
Genau hier setzt der Bereich Client Channels an. Im Fokus stehen zentrale digitale und physische Touchpoints zwischen der ZKB und ihren Kundinnen und Kunden, die Bedürfnisse mit Technologie, Prozessen, User Experience, Security und Betrieb verbinden. Dazu gehören unter anderem E\-Banking, Mobile Banking sowie digitale Eröffnungs\-, Onboarding\- und Lifecycle\-Prozesse.
Innerhalb von Client Channels verantwortet das Team ID Management \& API Banking den sicheren Zugang zu den digitalen Bankdienstleistungen der ZKB. Im Zentrum stehen das Customer Identity \& Access Management (CIAM), also die Verwaltung digitaler Kundenidentitäten und deren Zugriffsberechtigung, sowie die Open\-Banking\-Plattform. Fachteam und DevOps arbeiten eng zusammen und begleiten ihre Lösungen von der Konzeption bis zum stabilen Betrieb.
Für das fachseitige Team suchen wir dich als erfahrene Persönlichkeit an der Schnittstelle zwischen Business und IT.
**Deine Herausforderung**
* Aktive Mitgestaltung der Open\-Banking\-Plattform und der Lösungen für digitale Kundenidentitäten und deren Authentisierung
* Erhebung, Analyse und Modellierung fachlicher und technischer Anforderungen sowie Überführung in umsetzbare Features, User Stories, Spezifikationen und Testfälle
* Technische Leitung von Arbeitspaketen, Teilprojekten und parallel laufenden Vorhaben von der Konzeption bis zum Go\-live
* Enge Zusammenarbeit mit der Entwicklung und Unterstützung bei Testing, Rollouts und der Einführung neuer Lösungen
* Sicherstellung eines stabilen Betriebs sowie Einhaltung regulatorischer und sicherheitsrelevanter Anforderungen
* Regelmässige Übernahme der operativen Verantwortung inklusive Analyse und Koordination fachlicher und technischer Störungen im Second\- und Third\-Level\-Support
* Beratung interner und externer Partner zu Anforderungen, Machbarkeit, Abhängigkeiten und notwendigen Entscheidungen
**Deine Qualitäten und Begabungen**
* Abgeschlossenes Studium (Universität, FH) in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder ähnlich
* Mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung im technisch geprägten Business Engineering/Business Analyse, in der technischen Projektleitung oder im technischen Application Management
* Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im Customer Identity \& Access Management oder im plattformbezogenen Open\-Banking\- beziehungsweise Open\-Finance\-Umfeld
* Fähigkeit, Anforderungen so zu spezifizieren, dass Entwicklungsteams daraus konkrete Lösungen umsetzen können
* Erfahrung in Prozess\- und Datenanalyse sowie in Anforderungsermittlung und Modellierung, z.B. mit UML, BPMN oder Mock\-ups
* Gutes Verständnis für Backend\-Systeme, APIs, Authentifizierung und Security; Kenntnisse in OAuth, OpenID Connect oder Consent Management sind von Vorteil
* Erfahrung in der Koordination technischer Vorhaben und in agilen Arbeitsmodellen wie Scrum oder SAFe
* Analytische, eigenverantwortliche und teamorientierte Persönlichkeit mit ausgeprägtem Drive, klarer Kommunikation und Freude am Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern
* Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens C1\-Niveau sowie gute Englischkenntnisse

Dabei verbindest du technisches Verständnis mit konzeptioneller Stärke und begleitest deine Themen bis in den produktiven Betrieb. At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.
With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.
Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement.

We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it.
We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.
This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.
You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.
You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.
Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.

Carry multi-quarter programs
Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.
Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.
Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.
Own what gets specified and what ships
Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.
Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.
Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.
Protect revenue data integrity
Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.
Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.
Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.

s.h: In your first 6–12 months, you might
s.t:
Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.
Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.
Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.
Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.
Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.

s.h: What You'll Need to Be Successful
s.t:
Systems and domain depth
Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.
Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.
Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.
Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.
Program leadership
Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.
Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.
Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.
Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.
Judgment and communication
One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.
Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

As a Business Systems Analyst on Anthropic's BizTech team, you'll play a crucial role in bridging the gap between business needs and technical solutions. You'll translate complex business requirements into technical specifications and architectural decisions, ensuring engineering teams build solutions that scale with our rapid growth.

You'll work closely with stakeholders across the organization to understand their requirements, configure systems, and ensure our business technology ecosystem operates efficiently and effectively. This role combines analytical thinking with technical expertise to design, implement, and maintain systems that drive operational excellence.
You'll be responsible for analyzing business processes, gathering requirements, and translating them into technical solutions. As we continue to scale rapidly, you'll help ensure our systems and processes evolve to meet the growing demands of our organization while maintaining the high standards of efficiency and reliability that Anthropic requires.

Drive end-to-end delivery of technical projects from conception through launch
Configure and customize business systems to meet specific organizational needs, including user permissions, workflows, and integrations
Manage technical vendor evaluation for business applications, including contract negotiations, service level agreements, and ongoing vendor performance assessment
Create and maintain comprehensive system documentation, including process flows, user guides, configuration specifications, and technical documentation
Lead knowledge management initiatives to ensure institutional knowledge is captured, organized, and accessible to all team members
Own technical risk assessment and mitigation strategies
Analyze current business processes and identify opportunities for automation and optimization
Act as a liaison between technical teams and business users, translating complex technical concepts into user-friendly language
Conduct system testing, validation, and user acceptance testing for new implementations and updates
Provide ongoing support and training to end-users across the organization
Monitor system performance and usage metrics to identify areas for improvement
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure business systems integrate seamlessly with other platforms
Stay current with emerging technologies and industry best practices in business systems management

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. We launch new products, models and pricing often, and each launch has to work in our systems on day one. A seller needs to be able to quote it, Deal Desk needs to be able to approve it, billing needs to charge for it correctly, and Finance needs to report on it. This role owns how a launch gets into our quote-to-cash systems, from the first pricing conversation to the first invoice.
We are looking for someone who treats every launch as a change across many systems. You will join launch planning early, work out what has to change across catalog, quoting, contracts, billing, tax and reporting, and get all of it ready before the launch date.

You will build a good part of the Salesforce work yourself and partner with our Salesforce developers and Billing Engineering on the rest. You will be the named owner of the NPI process for systems, and the person Product, Pricing and Finance call when they want to know what it takes to launch something.
We are an AI-first systems team. You will use Claude as a normal part of how you design, build, test and document, and you will look for ways to make launches faster and more repeatable with AI.

Own the systems side of new product and pricing launches, from the first pricing discussion through launch day and the first billing cycle
Turn a pricing and packaging decision into concrete system changes: SKUs, price books, bundles, discount and approval rules, contract terms, billing plans, tax codes and reporting
Build and run a repeatable NPI playbook: intake, a readiness checklist, sign-offs, a launch calendar and a post-launch review
Join launch planning early with Product and Pricing. Push back on pricing ideas that cannot be quoted, billed or reported cleanly, and offer options that can
Design how new pricing models work end to end, including usage-based, seat-based, tiered, committed and multi-year ramp pricing, and which system is the source of truth for each part
Plan the impact on existing customers: moving customers to new SKUs, grandfathering, amendments and co-termination, and how renewals will work
Own end-of-sale and retirement of products and prices, so old SKUs leave the catalog without breaking renewals, billing or reporting
Coordinate the changes across Salesforce, billing and our tax platform, working with the teams who own each system
Partner with Deal Desk, Sales, Finance, Accounting, Tax and Legal so each team signs off on what changes for them before launch
Make sure sellers and Deal Desk are ready on launch day, including quote templates, approval paths, guidance and enablement
Check every launch after it goes live: do quotes, orders, invoices and Finance reports match? Add the control or reconciliation that catches the gaps
Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that is the right call, and write specs clear enough that developers can build the rest without several rounds of questions
Use AI to shorten launch cycles, for example generating catalog changes from a pricing spec, checking launch readiness, and testing quote and billing scenarios

Experience in GTM or revenue systems as a Business Systems Analyst, Q2C Systems Lead or similar role, with hands-on ownership of product and pricing launches
Experience launching new products or pricing models at a fast-growing company, owning the change across catalog, quoting, contracts and billing
Hands-on experience with Salesforce CPQ, Revenue Cloud or a similar CPQ tool, especially product and pricing data models, price books, bundles and approval rules
Working understanding of how a pricing decision flows into bookings, invoicing, tax and revenue recognition
Experience running a cross-functional process with many sign-offs (Product, Finance, Legal, Sales) and getting to launch on a fixed date
Hands-on Salesforce admin skills (Flow, validation rules, page layouts, approval processes) and comfort building meaningful parts of your own solution
Clear communication across Product, sellers, Deal Desk, Finance, Legal and engineers, adjusting the level of detail for each

Experience in GTM, revenue or finance systems roles
Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing, and with billing platforms such as Stripe, Metronome or Zuora
Experience moving existing customers onto new pricing, including migrations, grandfathering and amendments at scale
Experience with tax setup for new products (tax codes, tax engines such as Anrok or Avalara)
Experience with integrations between Salesforce and billing, ERP or provisioning systems, and comfort reading API payloads and integration logs
Basic SQL and comfort using a data warehouse to check launch data
Salesforce Administrator certification. CPQ Specialist, Advanced Administrator or Business Analyst certification is a plus
Hands-on use of AI tools (Claude or similar) in how you design, build or document systems, and the ability to explain how you check their output

We’re looking for a Business Systems Analyst to join our People Technology team in London. This is a full-time, hybrid role. You’ll support and evolve our Workday Time Tracking and/or Absence Management modules through configuration, project delivery and Tier 1 production support - ensuring a reliable, scalable experience for employees, managers, HR and Payroll teams.
Get to know our People team - what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.
You’ll report to the Senior Manager, Workforce Management. You’ll be the subject-matter expert for how Time Tracking and/or Absence is configured in our Workday tenant, translating business needs into scalable configuration and helping keep the system running smoothly for end users.

s.h: Here’s what your day-to-day might look like
s.t:
Own Workday Time and Absence Configuration: Gather and document requirements, configure Time Tracking and/or Absence Management, and support changes driven by new business needs, acquisitions or divestitures, and regulatory updates.
Deliver Robust Change and Release Management: Build and maintain functional designs and configuration workbooks; develop and execute unit, integration, regression and UAT test scripts; and assess the impact of Workday’s biannual releases.
Partner Across People, Payroll and Technology: Work with HR, Payroll and business stakeholders to validate time and absence data feeds into pay calculations, and support integrations with workforce-management tools, time clocks, scheduling tools and absence vendors.
Provide Tier 1 Production Support: Triage and resolve tickets involving missed punches, incorrect accruals, calculation errors and approval-routing issues. Distinguish configuration, data and integration problems, escalating to Tier 2/3 or Workday support where needed.
Improve the Employee Experience: Respond to employee and manager questions, monitor ticket trends, identify root causes and recommend proactive configuration fixes or process improvements.
Build Capability and Confidence: Create and maintain end-user documentation, job aids and training materials, and maintain clear service levels for ticket response and resolution.

Three or more years of hands-on Workday configuration experience in Time Tracking and/or Absence Management; Core HCM experience is a plus.
A solid understanding of Workday business processes, security groups and calculated fields as they relate to Time Tracking and Absence.
Experience gathering requirements, writing functional specifications and translating them into configuration.
Experience designing and executing test scripts, coordinating UAT and completing regression testing.
Strong troubleshooting skills across configuration, business-process logs and integration errors.
Experience using a ticketing system such as Jira, and the ability to balance project priorities with production-support requests.
Clear, confident communication skills with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Preferred experience includes Workday Time Tracking and/or Absence Management certification; experience with Legion, Calabrio, Deputy, time-clock/device integrations, third-party absence vendors, multi-country configurations or agile delivery.

DEPT® is looking for a Business Analyst who owns a workstream independently. A Senior Business Analyst at DEPT leads the translation of complex business needs into actionable product and technology solutions.

They'll work across clients, strategists, product managers, designers, engineers, and QA teams, to create alignment from discovery through delivery and ensure that solutions address the intended business and user outcomes, all with minimal oversight.

Our business analysts move between clients, industries, and delivery models, balancing client expectations against delivery constraints while working inside multidisciplinary agency teams.
GenAI fluency is core to this role, and you'll be expected to use AI tools daily, including drafting requirements and user stories, summarizing discovery sessions, generating first-pass documentation, all while applying the judgment built through years or rigor to critically review and correct the output, rather than trusting it blindly.

Additionally, a good candidate for this role should have a willingness to push the field forward, eager to create new ways of using these tools to build clarity for their teams.

Requirements and acceptance criteria for your workstream, start to finish
Traceability from business goals through requirements, stories, and delivered outcomes
Stakeholder alignment on scope and expected outcomes
UAT strategy, including scenarios, readiness criteria, and validation

Run Discovery: Lead stakeholder interviews and workshops, turning what you hear into clear, testable requirements and user stories.
Document Process & Gaps: Map current and future-state processes — flowcharts, personas, use cases, data mappings — and close gaps before they hit delivery.
Work the Team's Cadence: Follow Agile/Scrum or Kanban practices, adapting to the team's rhythm.
Resolve Stakeholder Conflict: Build trust-based relationships and resolve conflicting priorities directly, translating between technical and business language.
Define the Details: Business rules, data requirements, integrations, dependencies, and exception scenarios.
Mentorship: Guide junior team members on documentation standards and technique.

Independent Ownership: 2–4 years of BA experience, with a track record of owning a workstream independently rather than assisting under a senior BA.
Information Gathering & Documentation: Comfort running discovery and producing user stories, acceptance criteria, process diagrams, and functional specs.
Methodology: Working knowledge of Agile and the Software Development Lifecycle.
Tools: Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, Lucidchart, Miro, FigJam, and/or Adobe Workfront.
Platform Exposure: Familiarity with platforms like the Adobe stack (especially AEM), Salesforce (especially Commerce Cloud), and CMS platforms like Contentful or Optimizely a plus.
Agency Experience: Comfort moving between clients, industries, and delivery models in multidisciplinary teams, while balancing client expectations against delivery constraints. Ideal candidates will have experience working in Advertising.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, IT, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Clear Communication: Adjust the level of detail for executives, clients, or engineers as needed.
Facilitation & Curiosity: Run workshops that end in decisions, not just discussion, and ask the question that gets past the stated ask to the real problem.
Influence & Judgment: Build alignment through evidence and clear tradeoffs, and push back on unclear requirements or shaky solutions, respectfully but directly.
Ownership & Adaptability: Flag risks early, document decisions, and stay effective when priorities or teams shift under you.
Coaching: Give junior analysts real, actionable feedback.

Early Risk Detection: Risks, assumptions, and dependencies surface early.
Documentation: Decisions and changes are documented clearly.
UAT: Validates business outcomes, not just feature completion.
Mentorship: Junior analysts get consistent guidance and feedback.

We’re seeking a Senior Business Systems Analyst (BSA) to serve as a strategic liaison between IT and the business, driving scalable solutions that empower our Services and Education organizations . In this role, you’ll be responsible for designing, optimizing, and maintaining the business architecture and processes that support our teams through Professional Services Automation (PSA) , enabling them to quote, sell, deliver, and manage services with greater efficiency.
Leveraging your expertise in Salesforce and Certinia (FKA FinancialForce) PSA, you will collaborate with business partners, end users, and leadership teams to improve workflows, translate business needs into clear requirements, and deliver solutions that reflect simplicity and precision. You’ll take a strategic, data-driven approach to agile development and craft thoughtful technology roadmaps that balance current priorities with future scalability.
You are a curious problem-solver who’s not afraid to dive into complex systems, learn new tools, or explore how integrations can drive the PSA lifecycle forward. You proactively communicate, anticipate partner needs, and bring a passion for automation, efficiency, and detail. Your recommendations are thoughtful, well-informed, and lead to tangible business impact.

Serve as a subject-matter expert on Certinia (FKA FinancialForce) PSA, with strong functional knowledge across core features and related integrations.
Build and nurture strong relationships with key business stakeholders to establish a solid, trusted foundation for ongoing partnership and collaboration
Translate complex business needs into clear functional requirements; own requirements gathering, feature design, documentation, and end-user testing across enhancement requests and projects.
Apply a design-led mindset to partner with Services & Education Strategic Operations teams to optimize PSA; define enhancements and support ongoing maintenance.
Maintain a holistic view of business processes, users, and data flows to anticipate functional impacts of configuration updates, workflow changes, and reporting requirements.
Communicate complex system concepts in simple, approachable language through written materials, verbal communication, and visual presentations.
Develop and maintain system documentation, including configuration, data mapping, functional designs, test cases, and enablement materials.
Validate software quality by executing functional testing; collaborate with technical teams to identify and resolve defects and ensure solution aligns with business requirements.
Prepare clear documentation and presentations outlining current-state and future-state PSA processes and architecture.
Proactively identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve user experience, and deliver scalable automation; recommend solutions aligned with business goals and company strategy.
Contribute to cross-functional initiatives and IT projects; coordinate with BSAs and partners to ensure alignment, knowledge sharing, and coordinated delivery across domains.

5+ years experience in Business Systems Analysis & design on the Salesforce platform.
3+ years hands-on experience with Certinia (FKA FinancialForce) PSA.
Experience partnering with a Services organization to support delivery, enablement, and process optimization.
Experience designing, implementing, and supporting large-scale, complex Salesforce + PSA solutions in a production environment.
Hands-on expertise with PSA capabilities including Project Management, Resource Management, Time & Expense, Billing, and Revenue Recognition.
Familiarity with CPQ and Quote-to-Cash processes, particularly how quoting and order data integrate into PSA project structures; ability to partner with CPQ stakeholders to support upstream workflows.
Experience developing business processes and requirements for integrations with boundary systems (e.g., ERP such as NetSuite).
Broad and deep understanding of the Salesforce ecosystem, including data model, platform capabilities, and integrations.
Strong understanding of QA and UAT processes; able to define acceptance criteria, support functional validation, and partner with QA and business users to ensure successful testing outcomes.

Salesforce certifications (Admin, Business Analyst)
Certinia PSA certifications (Implementation Consultant, System Admin)

As Senior HR Tech & AI Automation Analyst, you will join the People & Organization Digital Transformation team as a bridge between HR and technology — deeply understanding how HR works end to end and translating business challenges into scalable technology, automation and AI solutions.
You will work across the hire-to-retire employee lifecycle, partnering with HR teams to challenge existing processes, identify opportunities for improvement and turn business needs into clear functional and technical requirements. You will then help take those solutions from idea through design, build and implementation — using our HR technology landscape, automation platforms and AI.
You will bring deep HR domain knowledge and hands-on technical capability to translate complex HR processes into scalable, technology-enabled solutions — from automation workflows and AI-powered tools to HRIS improvements and service delivery design.
The role reports to the Head of Digital Transformation, who is part of the HR Senior Leadership Team, and works closely with the People Enablement Tech stream, FlixTech, IT Security, Data Privacy and HR teams across all regions.
This role is based in Berlin. Given the global scope, regular collaboration with colleagues across European, APAC and US time zones is required.

Act as a trusted technology partner to HR teams across the end-to-end employee lifecycle — conduct process and technology gap analyses, challenge existing ways of working, identify improvement and automation opportunities, and translate business needs into functional and technical requirements implemented through HRIS, AI or automation solutions.
Help build, deploy and maintain Claude-based applications and AI-powered internal tools, working with our cloud and technology teams to ensure appropriate authentication (RBAC/ABAC), governance and HRIS-aligned access controls including MCPs, APIs and custom connectors that securely connect AI applications with the wider HR Tech landscape.
Design and build AI and automation workflows using technologies such as n8n, UiPath, Python-based automation and GenAI/LLMs, creating scalable solutions with appropriate orchestration, exception handling, monitoring and governance.
Drive HR Tech initiatives end to end, from requirements engineering and process/solution design through build, SIT/UAT, implementation and go-live across areas such as HR service delivery model, HRIS security model improvements, payroll transformations, HRIS revamp or migration.
Bring a strong product mindset to HR technology — turning business problems into scalable products and frameworks, including Jira-based HR service desks, Rovo Agents and AI-enabled employee/HR experiences, and continuously improving them based on user needs and business value.

6+ years of experience as an HR Tech Analyst, HR Business/Process Analyst, AI & Automation Analyst or similar role, with deep, demonstrable HR domain knowledge across hire-to-retire processes. This is must-have for the role. A degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, HR Technology, Business Technology or a related field is preferred.
Strong ability to analyse HR processes, translate business problems into functional and technical requirements, and implement solutions across a complex HR technology landscape.
Hands-on experience building AI and automation solutions using technologies such as n8n, Python scripts, UiPath and GenAI/LLM tooling. n8n certification is a plus.
Experience building and deploying internal applications in cloud environments, including working with APIs, MCPs, custom connectors and integrations to securely move data between enterprise systems.
Hands-on understanding of Claude/GenAI application deployment and enterprise security, including RBAC/ABAC, authentication, access governance and protection of sensitive HR data.
Strong working knowledge of Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Rovo Agents and BPMN, with the ability to design service desks, workflows, process frameworks and technology-enabled HR services.
Fluency in English. HR technology experience is essential; certifications in business/process analysis, automation or agile delivery (e.g. Six Sigma, SAFe, Scrum, PMP, Archimate) are a plus.

s.h: SENIOR ERP BUSINESS ANALYST I - MANUFACTURING & SUPPLY CHAIN
s.t: Based on-site at Rocket Lab's Headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Senior ERP Business Analyst I (SBA-I) is member of a global team responsible for supporting Rocket Lab ERP users and developing ERP supply chain and manufacturing solutions. You will work with other Business Analysts in the US and NZ under the direction of the ERP Team Lead and ERP Manager to help the global supply chain and manufacturing organizations to deliver exceptional performance through effective ERP systems.

Deliver outstanding support to the global supply chain and manufacturing teams using Rocket Lab LN ERP systems.
Work with existing ERP business & support analysts to design and deploy new ERP solutions and improvements to existing systems to support the growing Rocket Lab Business, manufacturing and supply chain goals.
Develop a deep knowledge of the Rocket Lab ERP systems to allow you to be one of the ERP teams application experts.
Enable the roll out of LN ERP systems across Rocket Lab and support the business in its LN Cloud migration project.
Ensure global ERP and business process standards are maintained, developed, and improved.
Build partnerships with operations, and engineering teams across Rocket Lab.

Bachlelor’s degree in business administration, engineering, or computer science.
5+ years proven experience supporting ERP manufacturing and supply chain users operating in hi-tech industries.

s.h: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY
s.t:
For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.
Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Samsara's Core IT team builds the systems, processes, and experiences that let every team at Samsara do its best work. As a Principal Business Systems Analyst, you'll own the programs with the broadest scope and highest impact on the team.

These are the ambiguous, cross-functional problems that touch multiple systems and multiple stakeholders, and that shape how Core IT operates going forward. You'll work directly with senior IT leadership and stakeholders across the business, and your frameworks and judgment will set the standard other analysts learn from.
This role is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C.. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You want to impact the industries that run our world. Your work will have real-world impact: helping keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and keep workers safe on the job.
You want to own problems, not just execute against ones someone else already scoped. At this level, you'll define the problem space for some of Core IT's most significant and ambiguous issues, and the frameworks and standards you build will be what other analysts learn from.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to keep growing. If you put in the work, this won't be your last role at Samsara. We've built a culture that rewards fast development and gives people real room to master their craft as the company keeps growing.
You want colleagues who make you better. You'll work alongside people who support each other's work, push each other to think more rigorously, and share the credit when something goes well.

Own end-to-end delivery of Core IT's highest-impact projects and programs, from problem definition through implementation, across multiple systems and business domains.
Define the problem space on the organization's most significant and ambiguous issues, rather than solving problems that are already scoped, and advise IT leadership on how to think about entire classes of problems, not just the issue in front of them.
Build the requirements practices, frameworks, and standards that other analysts and the broader team adopt, raising the bar for how Core IT approaches requirements, process design, and systems thinking.
Act as a trusted advisor to IT leadership and senior stakeholders across the business on organizational design, systems architecture, and process strategy.
Manage IT's engagement with the rest of the business on the programs you own: gathering requirements, coordinating resources, planning timelines, and communicating with stakeholders.
Drive operational excellence: develop a deep understanding of IT engineering, support, and operations (financials, services, performance metrics, SLAs, and so on) and work with IT management to provide the context that drives decision-making.
Develop, evaluate, and refine business processes, and propose improvement strategies that scale across the organization.
Mentor other analysts and engineers, and help them grow into the next level of scope and independence.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

10+ years of business systems analysis, strategy, or architecture experience at a large-scale organization.
Deep expertise in requirements strategy, organizational design, systems thinking, and process optimization, with mastery of the analytical disciplines behind them: data analysis, process optimization, and requirements architecture.
A demonstrated track record advising senior leadership on complex, strategic decisions, including experience with large-scale organizational transformation or system architecture decisions.

Excellent influence skills: the ability to build trust and move decisions forward with stakeholders and teams that don't report to you, from individual contributors to executive leadership.
Strong analytical rigor and the communication skills to bring senior stakeholders along, in writing and in the room.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex, concurrent programs end-to-end, with full independent judgment on how to structure and staff them.
Strong data management and analysis skills (Google Sheets/Excel, Splunk, and similar tools).
Experience with corporate security and compliance programs: operating internal controls, preparing evidence for audits, and ensuring proper data handling in response to requests under SOX, FedRAMP, GDPR, CCPA, or similar privacy regulations.

Lead end-to-end third-party security risk assessments — using both qualitative and quantitative methods — for Samsara's vendors and partners, and recommend risk ratings and tiering in line with Samsara's Vendor Risk Management Policy.
Own the vendor reassessment cadence and track remediation of any security gaps throughout the full lifecycle of the vendor.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, and system/relationship owners to review vendor contracts and onboarding requests submitted through Zip, ensuring security requirements (e.g. incident notification, data training, compliance, etc.) are in place before a vendor goes live.
Escalate unresolved vendor risk to Security leadership, legal, procurement, and business owners as necessary.
Support internal and external audits of the vendor risk program (e.g. ISO, SOC, FedRAMP).
Build and maintain the metrics, dashboards, and reporting that give Security leadership visibility into Samsara's third-party risk posture and program performance.
Support the GRC team's efforts to bring automation and AI-enabled tools into vendor risk workflows, such as using AI to triage vendor security questionnaires, flag high-risk contract terms, and incorporate industry learnings into the lifecycle.

Experience using automation, scripting, or low-code workflows to help scale a vendor risk program.
Hands-on experience running vendor security assessments and administering a vendor tiering program.
Experience partnering with Legal and Procurement on vendor contract security and privacy terms (e.g., Security addendums, DPAs, etc.).
Must reside in the US, outside the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, and Washington, D.C. metro areas.

Experience with a GRC or vendor risk management platform (e.g., Vanta, ServiceNow, OneTrust, Archer, or similar).
A relevant certification such as CTPRP, CISA, CRISC, or CISSP.
